rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a thermo-mechanical treatment (warm rolling + annealing) to induce serrated phase boundaries, while the target uses a high-pressure, high-temperature (HPHT) treatment to create a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room-temperature tensile testing of a eutectic HEA with a dual-phase lamellar microstructure, which matches the target's broad regime of room-temperature tensile deformation. However, the processing conditions (thermo-mechanical vs. HPHT) and the specific alloy (AlCoCrFeNi2.1 vs. Al0.7CoCrFeNi) differ.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes crack deflection and enhanced back-stress via serrated boundaries, while the target relies on coherent interfaces enabling dislocation transfer and hierarchical deformation mechanisms. These are different general classes of mechanism (crack-path tortuosity vs. dislocation-mediated plasticity accommodation).
rationale.outcome_agreement: Both predict simultaneous improvement in strength and ductility under room-temperature tension, which is the right property and direction. However, the hypothesis does not specify the magnitude of improvement, while the target reports a doubling of strength to ~1150 MPa and ductility to ~36%.
